title: Model-variant error-budget allocator and regional eviction playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Define and implement a per-model-variant error budget allocator and an operational playbook for regional eviction/load-shedding. The goal is to provide predictable degradation paths when capacity is constrained, enable safe cross-region borrowing of error budget, and wire the allocator into circuit-breaker triggers. Work includes SLI definitions (latency by token, success rate by semantic match for rerankers), the allocation algorithm, control-plane API, dashboarding, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator service exposes allocation decisions per endpoint and model variant via /api/v1/allocator (read-only) and can calculate remaining error budget on demand
Regional eviction rules must be expressible as policy: priority weight, minimum reserved headroom, and max borrow cap
Circuit-breaker thresholds tied to allocator state: when allocated remaining error budget < threshold and 95th latency quantile > configured SLI, fallback variants are selected automatically
Can simulate a full-region outage in staging and observe deterministic eviction and fallback behavior with <5% request loss compared to baseline test harness
Documentation and runbook published: Confluence doc + oncall checklist + a dashboard showing per-variant error budget burn and borrow events
notes: This ticket scopes algorithm design and control-plane integration; infra-level autoscaler changes are covered in ENG-51502.
We intentionally separate allocation decisions from execution to allow conservative rollouts and easy A/B testing of policies.
Primary SLIs chosen: token-p90 latency per route, request-level semantic success rate for reranking endpoints, and per-token server error rate. These map to composite SLOs using weighted aggregation.

Borrow model: short-term loan (lease) capped to 15% of borrower capacity, repayable within 10 minutes by throttling non-essential routes. Long-term borrow requires controller approval and will trigger paging. See design doc link below.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Aisha Raman: Initial spec checked in. Added SLI candidates and high-level acceptance criteria. Asked infra to reserve a staging cluster for simulation (cc: @infra).

2025-02-18 - Marco Li: Spike complete — basic allocator prototype can compute weighted budgets using recent burn rate and priority weights. Observed oscillations when using a pure exponential smoothing window; propose adding minimum lease windows to avoid flapping.
2025-02-21 - Design review (Anika Patel): Suggested adding explicit UX hooks in Console to show borrow requests before they execute so SREs can pre-approve emergency borrows.

2025-02-25 - PR #4212 opened (runtime allocator core). Requesting review from @sre-team and @platform-api. Integration tests failing on a race between allocator refresh and autoscaler signal; adding short mutex in control plane to reduce race surface.

2025-02-27 - Engineering sync: Decided on two-tier borrow: immediate short lease (<=10m) auto-granted if <15% of capacity requested, else operator approval required. Added operator override for canary endpoints.
2025-03-01 - Load-shedding policy added: non-critical routes (label: background) can be evicted first. Need to add route-label propagation to the gateway (assigned to ENG-50117).
2025-03-03 - Security review note (TBD): KMS usage not impacted; audit logs must include allocator decisions. Margaret (security) requested schema for audit entries — created follow-up ENG-52580.

implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize SLI mapping and priority weight schema. Draft Confluence API contract for allocator service.
Week 2: Implement allocator core + unit tests. Wire allocator endpoint into control plane read path.
Week 3: Integrate allocator decision into router fallback logic and circuit-breaker hooks. Add dashboard panels for burn and borrow events.
Week 4: Run staging chaos tests (region loss, traffic spike), iterate on thresholds, and publish runbook. Start gradual canary in runtime-1.19.
Post-release: Monitor error budget behavior for 2 weeks and adjust smoothing parameters if oscillation persists.
risks: Oscillation between regions if allocator decisions are too aggressive — mitigated by minimum lease windows and damping factor
Over-borrowing by noisy tenants leading to silent degradation for higher-priority customers — mitigated by per-tenant caps and operator alerts
Increased control-plane latency if allocator compute is heavy — mitigated by caching and precomputation windows
